messages:
liam: heads-up — after yesterday's continuous-batcher tweak i'm seeing a p95 spike for tiny prompts (1-2 tokens). throughput on rtx-pool-3 dropped ~12%

devon: saw that too, noticed kernel selection flipped to generic on a lot of small batches. KV miss rate on those hosts jumped concurrent with the rollout :thinking:

sara: do we have traces? small threads are noisy but the pattern looks like first-token delay inflation -> selector chooses more conservative kernel

liam: attaching profiler excerpt below, trimmed: 

```
2026-03-17T22:12:34Z host=rtx-pool-3 batch_id=0x7f2 kernel_selected=matmul_generic -> slow_path
kv_miss=true first_token_delay_ms=13.8 total_latency_ms=92.1 batch_size=2 token_budget=128
```

devon: that first_token_delay is the smoking gun. Two possibilities: (1) prefill change caused KV priming to kick in and GC churn increased, or (2) batch formation now mixes shapes in a way that triggers fallback kernels.

liam: i captured scheduler dump for a reproducer run: 

```
# scheduler dump
enqueue t=2203456789 qlen=1 wait=12ms
batch formed sizes=[1,2] shapes=[8,16] -> coalesced -> chosen kernel=matmul_generic (prefill_penalty evaluation: -0.02)
```

sara: note: we lowered prefilling penalty in the heuristic tweak to reduce cold-start latency. that should bias toward fast kernels, not generic. weird.

deploy-bot: deploy 5f3a1c2 -> continuous-batcher service (canary: rtx-pool-3)

devon: i ran a local experiment toggling KV TTL to simulate priming: 
- kv.ttl=1s -> kv_miss_rate ~42% -> p95 ~180ms
- kv.ttl=60s -> kv_miss_rate ~3% -> p95 ~44ms

liam: so kv_miss_rate correlates strongly. hypothesis: the selector's feature vector lacked kv_miss_rate, so with prefilling_penalty lowered we actually increased prefill attempts -> more short-lived keys -> GC thrash -> higher miss rate -> selector flips to safe kernel. net effect: higher latency.

sara: good find. mitigation options: revert prefilling tweak (fast), add kv_miss_rate into selector (medium), or change cache priming window to avoid heavy GC churn (longer). we should do a quick rollback to stop customer impact.

liam: i'm starting rollback now on canary and will patch selector to include kv_miss_rate as a tie-breaker. also adding metric `kernel_route_reason` and `kv_miss_rate_per_batch` for visibility.

devon: filed issue #4289 with traces, perf graphs, and reproducer script: https://redwood/issue/4289

sara: nice. add a small CI microbenchmark that forces kv miss scenarios so we can't regress silently in the future. also add an alert when `kv_miss_rate_per_batch` > 20% for small batches.

liam: rollback complete on canary (rtx-pool-3). preliminary p95 back to baseline. will monitor for 30m then roll forward with selector change behind a feature flag.

devon: thumbs up. when you roll forward, also try a gradual prefill_rate ramp instead of all at once.

sara: thanks team. follow-up tasks: revert PR id=... (done), new PR to include kv_miss_rate to selector, add CI microbenchmark, alert dashboard update.

liam: ping me if you see any >100ms p95 on tiny prompts.

sara: will do, closing thread once canary stable. :white_check_mark:
